newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH AFRICA - OCT 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH AFRICA - OCT 15.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Financial institutions are offering funding to certain business members of the National Empowerment Consortium which would allow them to buy Anglo's stake in Johnnic through preference and ordinary shares -- with a condition that the NEC agrees to unbundle Johnnic.
- Violence and underground fires took their toll at gold mines managed by Gold Fields of South Africa in the September quarter, reducing pre-capex profit 23 percent to 275 million rand.

- Fresh attempts would be made to negotiate an overarching social accord on growth, despite major differences between key social partners at the National Economic, Development and Labour Council (Nedlac), labour sources said yesterday.

- Government was steering away from its 60 to 90 billion rand "grand 10-year plan" for the provision of municipal infrastructure, towards a year-on-year spending programme, constitutional development director-general Andrew Boraine said yesterday.

- The Medical Research Council told Parliament yesterday that almost 50,000 South African women had backstreet abortions every year which cost the country millions in post abortion treatment, while "pro-lifers" challenged the ANC to hold a national referendum on the issue.

- Gold Fields of South Africa's gold division posted sharply lower profit for the September quarter yesterday, citing out-of-control mine violence and underground fires which many suspect were the result of arson and troubled industrial relations.

- A survey of the leadership styles of black executives has debunked some myths about black chief executives, indicating that their behaviour in most cases is similar to that of their white counterparts.
- The labour department has launched an investigation into the "slave wages" workers allege are paid in the clothing industry.

- The European Investment Bank (EIB), the international lending arm of the European Union, has launched the sale of 100 million rand in five-year bonds, denominated in rands, to European investors, Hambros Bank, the lead manager, said yesterday.

- Naledi Media Investments, a consortium of black business interests, local pension funds and overseas investors, is seeking an interdict to prevent the Independent Broadcasting Authority (IBA) from issuing the broadcasting licence for Radio Jacaranda to Newshelf 71 until the IBA's decision has been reviewed by the court.
- A bullish Andre Markgraaff -- vying with Louis Luyt as the most hated rugby man in Gauteng -- yesterday rounded on his critics.
- The quadruple family killing in which three Reiger Park children were shot dead by their father before he killed himself was carried out with a weapon police had earlier given back to the killer.
